page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7a.xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7T83 processor built on x86_64 architecture and running under the KVM hypervisor. The virtual machine delivers 4 dedicated vCPUs spanning 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core, operating at a base frequency of 2.55 GHz. Memory capacity is allocated at 8.0 GB, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The cache topology includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. Supported hardware features include AES, VAES, SHA-NI, AVX, and BMI2 instruction sets, while AVX-512 and AMX extensions are not available on this CPU model.

Hardware bundling does not include local disk storage, necessitating network-attached storage volumes for persistent data. Baseline network bandwidth is provisioned at 2 Gbps, and no GPUs are attached. In synthetic benchmarking, the server demonstrates strong single-core compute performance in stress-ng tests, ranking in the top quartile. However, multi-core throughput in both stress-ng and Geekbench tests drops to lower quartiles, reflecting the four-thread envelope. Memory bandwidth performance shows lower-tier throughput across uncached reads at 31.27 GB/sec and uncached writes at 15.45 GB/sec, while single-threaded compression and cryptographic operations deliver steady, mid-range throughput.

Given the balance of dedicated AMD execution threads and a compact memory footprint, the instance offers a resource-efficient posture for CPU tasks with modest memory footprints. Tradeoffs include the absence of onboard NVMe storage, limited baseline networking, and reduced parallel memory bandwidth. Consequently, the configuration is appropriate for stateless web application serving, batch processing tasks, light CI/CD workers, and API microservices rather than large in-memory databases or parallelized data science workloads.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7a.xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 7T83 processor at 2.55 GHz on x86_64 architecture. The server delivers 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores paired with 8.0 GB of RAM, conforming to a 1:2 compute memory profile. No local storage is bundled, and network throughput provides a 2 Gbps baseline. Performance evaluations demonstrate strong single-core CPU throughput in stress-ng testing alongside standard encryption speeds, balanced against lower multi-core scaling and uncached memory bandwidth. Without local NVMe disks or GPU acceleration, this instance is configured as a cost-efficient platform for light and medium computational workloads that fit within an 8.0 GB boundary. Practical implementations include frontend web hosting, microservices, background job workers, and batch processing pipelines.
